name: Mu2e detector
notes: technology_classes uses 'spectrometer': the detector's function (momentum/energy analysis of a mono-energetic conversion electron via tracker + calorimeter behind a solenoidal magnet chain) is closer to a spectrometer than to any of the other listed classes (none of which name a solenoidal charged-lepton spectrometer specifically).

length.note: Overall solenoid-system length not stated in any fetched source (2026-09-18 verification removed an unsupported 25 m quote).

summary.plain: A 25-metre chain of giant superconducting magnets at Fermilab, with a tracker and a fast crystal detector at the end, built to catch the single electron that would appear if a muon ever turned into one.
summary.technical: Production, transport and detector superconducting solenoids (25 m combined length) with a straw-tube tracker and fast CsI crystal calorimeter behind the stopping target, plus a cosmic ray veto system covering the solenoids, per the Mu2e TDR and subsequent status reports. Under construction; no data yet.

technology.quote: The system comprises production, transport, and detector solenoids, with downstream straw tracker and crystal calorimeter.
technology.value: A 25-metre chain of three superconducting solenoids (production, transport, detector) feeding a straw-tube tracker and a fast CsI crystal calorimeter, surrounded by a cosmic-ray veto
